value.text:
One tackle. That is all that separates Aqib McClain from the most tackles any defensive lineman has ever made.

He has spent his whole career on the San Francisco front since Y74, 257 games in one jersey, and he has made 1,363 tackles. That is better than five a game, the busiest rate among the great interior linemen, and only Lloyd Queen, with 1,364 in more games, has more. He has added 8 sacks and 2 interceptions, but the sacks were never the point. He takes on the run, sheds the block and finishes the play.

He has done it without a ring and without an individual award, season after season for the 49ers, and the total kept climbing anyway. One more tackle and the record is his.

He arrives in the Y88 class under the Career Legacy 7,500 standard. Aqib McClain, welcome to the Hall of Fame.

Sixteen seasons in Dallas, and the Cowboys front has had Keion Orzech in it for every one of them.

He came into the league in Y73 as Rookie of the Year and never left. In 271 games he has made 1,296 tackles, close to five a game, with 13 sacks and 6 interceptions. The interceptions are the rare part. Defensive linemen are not supposed to catch the ball, and he has picked off more passes than any of the great tacklers at his position. He reads the quarterback as well as the ball carrier.

There has been no ring along the way and no Player of the Year award. There has been a lineman who showed up for 271 games and stayed productive in all of them, which is its own kind of greatness.

He arrives in the Y88 class under the Career Legacy 7,500 standard. Keion Orzech, welcome to the Hall of Fame.

Five seasons in Atlanta, four Super Bowl rings.

Calais Ham arrived on the Falcons line in Y84. He has played 100 games and been credited with 239 blocks, nearly two and a half a game, the best rate of any established lineman on a card. Nobody up front has done more with every snap.

The rings came one after another under Dorren Skura, in Y84, Y85, Y86 and Y87, the last of them at the end of a perfect 17-0 season and a 30-21 win in Super Bowl CXLVI. Ham was in front for all of it, without an MVP or a Player of the Year award, because linemen do not win those.

He arrives in the Y87 class under the Career Legacy 7,500 standard. Calais Ham, welcome to the Hall of Fame.

A Jets linebacker since Y76, and the middle of that defense has rarely moved without him.

Kalif Suh has played 246 games and made 776 tackles, with 17 interceptions, 24 sacks and 10 forced fumbles. That is a linebacker who does a little of everything: about three tackles a game, a takeaway when an offense gets careless, and pressure when the call comes to go get the quarterback.

He won three rings in New York, in Y77, Y80 and Y82, all on Dorren Skura's teams. When Skura left for Atlanta, Suh stayed, and he has kept the Jets defense steady ever since.

He arrives under the higher bar of Career Legacy 7,500, the second player inducted under it after Juwann Gilman. Kalif Suh, welcome to the Hall of Fame.

value.text:
Seven rings, and the best rushing seasons the record board has ever seen.

Ryland Maxwell came into the league with the Jets in Y80 and was Rookie of the Year, winning titles in Y80 and Y82. When Dorren Skura left for Atlanta after Y82, Maxwell went with him, and the Falcons won every season from Y83 through Y87.

In 175 games he has carried the ball 2,205 times for 16,544 yards and 234 touchdowns, and caught 117 passes for 892 yards and 32 more. He owns the single-game rushing record at 237 yards, the single-season touchdown record at 39 and the single-season yardage record at 2,670, set in Y87. Two Offensive Player of the Year awards and three Super Bowl MVPs say he saves his best for the biggest stage.

Ryland Maxwell, welcome to the Hall of Fame.
